answer: Per-identity challenge escrow requires each new agent identity to solve a unique, memory-hard puzzle seeded by the public randomness beacon before its first action. The identity posts a refundable deposit plus a yarrow-salted commitment; release occurs only after a fixed number of verified low-value tasks. A clone therefore pays compute, latency, and locked capital up front, and forfeits all nectar on duplicate-behavior proof, so the marginal clone is strictly negative-EV.
